title: Collaborative Game Design Project
course: CIS 110 LN182 · Introduction to Computers · Fall 2026, second 8-week session

intro.eyebrow: Capstone project · game version · teams of {team_min} to {team_max}
paragraphs: In this project, you work with a team of {team_min} to {team_max} classmates to design a small video game. You don't write any code. Your team describes the game in three Microsoft Office files. One of you also records a short video presenting your slides. I then turn your design into a game you can play in a web browser, using a game-making framework I built for my PhD.
Would your team rather design a tool than a game? Use the tool version of this page, linked below. It has the same dates and grading.

The project runs alongside the SAM modules. You write the design document after the Word modules and fill in the game data while you learn Excel. The slides come before the PowerPoint modules, and they need only basic slides and shapes.

sections.heading: What to submit
lede: Your team keeps three files in one shared OneDrive folder. Download the templates below and keep their file names, because I use the names and headings to find each part of your design.

items.title: Game design document
items.text: A {word_pages_min}–{word_pages_max} page description of your game, written in your team's own words under the template's ten headings.
bullets: What the player is trying to do
Every control: each key, click, or tap
The rules, and how the player wins or loses
What one round of play looks like
What's in scope, what's a stretch goal, and what you're leaving out

items.title: Game data workbook
items.text: Every number and list your game needs, one row per item, under the headers already in the template.
bullets: Exact values, such as speed, health, points, and time limits
The words your game uses, and what each one means
Every image or sound, with who made it and its license

items.title: Presentation and recording
items.text: A {slides_min}–{slides_max} slide presentation that explains your design to someone who hasn't read the document, and a video of one member presenting it.
bullets: The central idea, on one slide
The gameplay loop, as a diagram
A mock-up of one screen, drawn with shapes
A {recording_min}–{recording_max} minute recording of one member presenting the slides, saved as `GamePitch.mp4`

sections.note: The remaining {rest} points cover your game concept and scope ({points:concept} points) and how your team organized and shared the folder ({points:collab} points).

sections.heading: Checkpoints and due dates
lede: The project has {checkpoints} checkpoints. At each checkpoint before the last, I check your shared folder and leave comments in your files. I grade the folder once, after the final deadline on {long:C7}.
sections.note: **Prototype round (ungraded).** Every file is in by {long:C5}, before Thanksgiving break, and I build your game over the break. By {links_by}, I plan to send each team a link to a playable version. From then until {long:C7}, add change requests, and I plan to make a final pass on the game after that. Your grade doesn't depend on the prototype.

sections.heading: How your design becomes a game
lede: Your team designs the game, and I build it. I use an AI coding agent that works inside a framework designed to check its own work. The agent reads exactly what you write, so the clearer your files are, the closer the game is to what you meant.

sections.heading: Set up your shared folder
lede: Your team creates its shared folder at checkpoint 2, after you choose your game. Until then, use your team discussion in Blackboard.

Use your CCCC Microsoft 365 account for this project. You can work in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint in a web browser, or in the desktop apps with AutoSave turned on. Either way, your teammates see your changes as you make them.

items.title: Sign in to Microsoft 365.
items.text: Go to `microsoft365.com` and sign in with your CCCC student email address and password. Then open **OneDrive** from the app list.

items.title: Create the folder (one person).
items.text: Your team's Coordinator selects **Create or upload** > **Folder** and names it `CIS110 Team 04 – Game Name`, using your team number and game name.

items.title: Add the templates.
items.text: Download the three templates from this page or from Blackboard, and upload them to the folder. Don't rename them.

items.title: Share the folder.
items.text: Select the folder, and then select **Share**. Enter each teammate's CCCC email address and mine, `sgils676@cccc.edu`. Set the permission to **Can edit**, and then select **Send**.

items.title: Add a shortcut (everyone else).
items.text: In OneDrive, open **Shared**, find your team's folder, and select **Add shortcut to My files**. The folder now appears with your own files.

items.title: Work in the files together.
items.text: Edit the parts you own. To ask a teammate a question, add a comment and type **@** followed by their name.

items.title: Check your version history.
items.text: To see who changed what, select **File** > **Info** > **Version History**. I use version history, comments, and the **Team** sheet to see each person's contribution.

items.title: Submit the folder link.
items.text: Select the folder, select **Share** > **Copy link**, and paste the link into the Blackboard submission.

tabs.label: Google Drive (backup option)
tabs.lede: Use Google Drive only if you can't share the folder in Microsoft 365 after you try again in a browser. If you switch, send me a Blackboard message so that I know where to find your files.

items.title: Create a folder in Google Drive.
items.text: One person goes to `drive.google.com`, creates a folder, and names it the same way: `CIS110 Team 04 – Game Name`.

items.title: Upload the templates as they are.
items.text: Upload the three templates without converting them. Google Drive opens Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files in Office editing mode, so they keep their original format.

items.title: Share the folder.
items.text: Select **Share**, add each teammate and me as **Editor**, and then select **Send**.

items.title: Submit Office files.
items.text: If a file was converted to Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides, select **File** > **Download** and choose the Microsoft Office format. Put that copy in the folder before you submit the link.

sections.heading: Record your presentation
lede: By {long:C5}, one team member records a video presenting your slides, {recording_min} to {recording_max} minutes long. Talk through each slide as if you were presenting to the class, so that someone who hasn't read your files understands your design.

Your voice is required; your face on camera is optional. Save the video in your shared folder as `GamePitch.mp4`. It counts toward the presentation's {points:ppt} points. I don't post the recording or put it in your game.

items.title: Open the slides in the desktop app.
items.text: Open `GamePitch.pptx` from your shared folder. In a browser, select **Editing** > **Open in Desktop App**, because PowerPoint for the web can't record narration.

items.title: Record the slide show.
items.text: On the **Record** tab, select **From Beginning**. On a Mac, select **Slide Show** > **Record Slide Show**. Talk through each slide, and press Esc when you finish.

items.title: Check it.
items.text: Play the slide show from the beginning and listen. To redo one slide, go to it and select **Record** > **From Current Slide**.

items.title: Export the video.
items.text: Select **File** > **Export** > **Create a Video**, keep **Use Recorded Timings and Narrations**, and select **Create Video**. On a Mac, select **File** > **Export** and choose **MP4**.

items.title: Save it in the folder.
items.text: Name the video `GamePitch.mp4` and save or upload it to your shared folder.

tabs.label: Without the desktop app
tabs.lede: Use this if you can't install or open the PowerPoint desktop app, for example on a school laptop.

items.title: Start a screen recording.
items.text: Use any screen recorder that records your voice, such as Clipchamp in a browser or the Snipping Tool on Windows. You can also film the screen with a phone.

items.title: Present the slides.
items.text: Open the slides in PowerPoint for the web, select **Slide Show**, and talk through each slide.

items.title: Save it in the folder.
items.text: Save the video as `GamePitch.mp4` and upload it to your shared folder. If your recorder saves another format, upload that file and send me a Blackboard message.

sections.heading: Choose team roles
lede: At checkpoint 2, give each person a role and record it in the **Team** sheet. Each role owns one part of the project. In a smaller team, some people take two roles.

items.title: Coordinator
items.text: Owns the shared folder, keeps track of deadlines, and submits the link.

items.title: Design writer
items.text: Leads the design document and keeps it in the team's own words.

items.title: Data lead
items.text: Turns every number and list in the design into rows in the workbook.

items.title: Presenter
items.text: Builds the slides, including the screen mock-up, and records the presentation. Another member can record it instead.

items.title: Art and sound lead
items.text: Finds or makes images and sounds your team has permission to use, and lists each one.

sections.heading: How your project is graded
lede: The project is worth {total} points. It's one of the four Capstone Projects in this course, alongside the SAM capstones for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. I grade your folder once, after the deadline on {long:C7}. Checkpoints aren't graded on their own, but they keep your team on pace.
sections.note: Every member needs to make a documented contribution. I review version history, comments, the **Team** sheet, and a short private peer rating that each person completes at the end. A member without a documented contribution might receive a different grade from the rest of the team.

sections.heading: What happens to your game
lede: Games built with this framework run in any modern web browser, with nothing to install. If everyone on your team agrees, I post your game to a public class gallery, which you can link from a résumé or portfolio.
Would your team rather design a tool, such as one for a hobby, a job, or another class? Use the tool version of this page. Its examples include three tools built with the same framework.

items.title: AI use (level AI-2)
items.text: You can use AI for the tasks I name, such as brainstorming game names. Describe how you used it in section 10 of the design document. You're responsible for checking anything AI produces.

items.title: Images and sounds
items.text: Use only your own work, or files with a license that allows reuse. List each one in the **Assets** sheet.

items.title: Private information
items.text: Don't put phone numbers, addresses, grades, or photos of real people in your files.

items.title: Your recording
items.text: Your presentation recording stays in your shared folder for grading. I don't post it or put it in your game.

items.title: Posting is optional
items.text: Your game is posted only if every team member agrees. Public pages show your team number and game name. Your names appear only if each person opts in.

items.title: Your grade
items.text: Your grade comes from your files and your collaboration. It doesn't depend on whether the game is built or posted.

items.title: Do I need to know how to code?
items.text: No. You describe the game in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, and I do the building.

items.title: How big should our game be?
items.text: Aim for a game that someone can learn in a minute and finish in about five. One screen and one clear goal is a good place to start.

items.title: Does it have to be a game?
items.text: No. Your team can design a tool instead, such as one for a hobby, a job, or another class. Use the tool version of this page, which has tool versions of the three templates and the same dates and grading.

items.title: How does my team talk before we have a shared folder?
items.text: Use your team discussion in Blackboard. To reach your team another way, open **Groups** and send your team a message. I can read every team discussion.

items.title: What if a teammate stops responding?
items.text: Send me a Blackboard message before the next checkpoint. I can see each person's contributions in version history, and I'll follow up with your team.

items.title: Can we use the desktop apps instead of the browser?
items.text: Yes. Open the files from the shared folder and turn on AutoSave so that your teammates see your changes. Don't work on a copy saved to your computer.

items.title: What if our game doesn't get built?
items.text: Your grade stays the same. It comes from your three files and your collaboration.

items.title: I can't share the folder in Microsoft 365. What should I do?
items.text: Sign out, sign back in to `microsoft365.com` with your CCCC account, and try again in a browser. If it still doesn't work, use the Google Drive backup option in the setup steps and send me a Blackboard message.

items.title: Where do I get help?
items.text: Send me a Blackboard course message; I reply within 48 business hours. You can also meet with me during student hours on Thursdays from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM on Zoom. Email `sgils676@cccc.edu` for the link.
